rule: A project is limited in time (for example up to 4 years), has a team, a fixed budget (for example 3,000-450,000 EUR) and a unique result.
Before applying, check four things: do you meet the call requirements, can you co-finance from your own funds, can you take on long-term commitments, and do you have a team.
Some funds cover only part of the budget, or top up international funding you already have. Check whether you can contribute your own funds.
A project moves through identification (initiation), planning, implementation (management), closure and evaluation, with monitoring and control throughout.

An application is the implementation plan born in the initiation phase. It usually covers the problem, the solution (activity plan), schedule, risks, budget, sustainability, benefit and impact, communication, and team.
In a direct call, the organisation submits its own application to the fund or programme administrator.
Many calls repeat every year or several times a year. Check deadlines before planning.
Where the main beneficiary is already designated, other organisations join through partnerships, procurement or separate calls.
Check first: NGO Fund, SADM calls, CERV, Erasmus+, ESF+. Then also: Swiss programme, Interreg, private funds.

topic: Pre-screening by applicant type, culture organisations
rule: Culture organisations check first: LKT, Creative Europe, Nordic Culture Point. Then also: Interreg, CERV, Baltic Culture Fund.

topic: Pre-screening by applicant type, education institutions
rule: Education institutions check first: Erasmus+, Nordplus, ESF+. Then also: Interreg, Swiss programme, the municipality.

topic: Pre-screening by applicant type, sports organisations
rule: Sports organisations check first: National Sports Agency, Erasmus+ Sport. Then also: the municipality, Interreg, private sponsors.

topic: Pre-screening by applicant type, social service institutions
rule: Social service institutions check first: ESF+, SADM calls, CERV. Then also: Erasmus+, Interreg, the municipality.
Municipalities check first: EU investments, Interreg, CERV. Then also: Creative Europe, Erasmus+, regional programmes.

topic: Pre-screening is only a first filter
rule: The applicant-type table is a first screen. Always read the conditions of the specific call.
Lithuanian eligibility differs from one Nordic programme to another.
A large share of Swiss-Lithuanian programme funds is implemented through pre-defined projects, so open calls are limited.
Assess Lithuanian conditions for the new period only once official calls are published. Projects can run until 2031.
Corporate support calls are usually short and thematic. Treat them as a supplementary source, not a base source.
To receive 1.2% PIT allocations and use donation platforms, the organisation needs the right support recipient status (paramos gavėjo statusas). Suits continuity and smaller initiatives.
Check each foundation's priorities and application procedure on its website.
LAG calls are often open only to NGOs registered in the LAG territory. Some require community organisations that have operated in the territory for at least one year.

Social business is an EU priority; the Commission presented the Social Economy Action Plan in 2022. Many LAGs support setting up a social business, usually on condition of creating at least 1 job. Advice: LISVA, Inovacijų agentūra, "Geri norai", Innovate, business programmes at "Spiečius" coworking centres, LAGs.
Project ideas must target the group defined in the AID2 financing conditions (point 7.1.3) and cover the activities in points 5.1.1.1 and 5.1.2.1. Submit via the application form from 23 March 2026.

KA210: at least 2 organisations from 2 programme countries. KA220: at least 3 organisations from 3 programme countries. Alliances for Innovation: 8-12 applicants from 4-8 countries with education and labour market partners. CoVE: at least 8 applicants from 4 countries, each with a VET provider and an employer.

The main 2026 deadline for KA210 and KA220 was 5 March 2026. Youth-field small-scale and cooperation partnerships were still open in Lithuania until 1 October 2026. For other education fields, prepare for the 2027 call.
Read the Programme Guide for the year before writing: it sets priorities, eligible activities, requirements for organisations and activities, and funding rules.
Use the EPALE Partner Search and the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform to find partners and past projects.

Public bodies (municipalities, schools, universities, research institutes) and NGOs or non-profits can apply. Private entities can only be partners; the lead beneficiary must be public or non-governmental.

Cross-border programmes cover specific regions: Lithuania-Poland covers border municipalities such as Alytus, Marijampolė and Vilkaviškis; Latvia-Lithuania covers northern Lithuania (Panevėžys, Biržai, Šiauliai) and neighbouring Latvian regions.

LIFE applications go to the European Commission through the Funding & Tenders portal. Calls are annual. Strategic integrated projects are prepared in two stages: concept, then full proposal. The LIFE programme document sets objectives, project types and evaluation criteria.

Useful listings: esinvesticijos.lt (calls plan, calls, projects), the NIPC portal and 3sektorius.lt for NGO funding, the SPPD list of 2026 calls, JRA funding calls, municipal websites, cerv.lt, kurybiskaeuropa.eu, solidarumokorpusas.lt, erasmus-plius.lt, norden.lt, esbendradarbiavimas.lt, lifeprojektai.lt, cpva.lt, norwaygrants.lt.
Start from the call document: guidelines for applicants (Gairės pareiškėjams), the funding conditions description (finansavimo sąlygų aprašas) or the competition regulations (konkurso nuostatai).
Read the selection criteria first and see what earns points. Then check your commitments, the financial conditions, and whether you have the team and partners.
Plan the project as a chain: relevance and importance show the problem, objectives and activities show the idea and how it will be done, results show the benefit.
Call priorities can fix minimum budget shares for certain activities, for example at least 50% for rights defence and at least 5% for a priority activity. Check these before you plan the budget.
Municipal NGO calls list the activity areas they fund. The project must fit one of them.
In the SADM institutional strengthening call, the project must pursue one of six listed strengthening directions.
Test the idea on a non-expert: would your neighbour understand the project?

Back the need with evidence: scientific articles, open data (Registrų centras, State Data Agency), strategic documents and national programmes (e-seimas). AI tools can help with research and planning.
Be specific. Replace general claims with numbers and say where they come from (how many members, how many lonely seniors, what services exist, survey results).
Keep the logic tight. Every planned activity must answer a problem described in the needs section; unrelated activities weaken the proposal.
Use a work breakdown structure (WBS): split the work into phases, then parts of phases, then detailed work packages.
Use a Gantt chart to show each task on a timeline: what must be done, when it starts and ends, how long it lasts, and how tasks depend on each other. Free templates exist (Office, TeamGantt).
AI planning tools such as Taskade can draft a WBS for a project.

A cost is eligible if it is directly linked to project activities, incurred during the project period, real and at market price, reasonable and efficient, and recorded in the accounts so it can be identified and checked with documents.

Split activity costs into administration costs (project administrator, accountant, admin communication, premises and utilities, bank fees) and implementation costs (team salaries, external experts, team communication, travel, services, goods). Indirect costs are a separate question.

Not eligible: proposal preparation, costs before submission, volunteer work, debts and late fees, fines and legal costs, used goods, luxury items or over-specified equipment, first or business class flights (unless justified), salaries for staff not working on the project, staff entertainment, bonuses, severance, overtime and holiday work, extra pension contributions, credits to third parties, and anything already paid by another project.

Justify salary rates with historical data (employment contract, payroll certificate), Ministry of Finance fixed rates, average market pay by position (State Data Agency, manoalga.lt), or the organisation's internal pay rules.

Justify services and goods with past invoices or contracts, Ministry of Finance fixed rates (fuel, events), the ESFA market price analysis (cite the item), supplier websites, supplier surveys or commercial offers. One offer is often enough; some calls ask for two, or only above a set amount.
Each salary line should state the position, planned hours (days or months), the average hourly rate including employer taxes and its basis, and a clear calculation.

Add annual leave or unused leave compensation using the Ministry of Finance fixed rate: 8.62% for 20 working days of leave (normal 5-day week), 11.01% for 25 days (staff under 18, single parents of a child under 14 or a disabled child under 18, disabled staff).
Budget salaries as the full workplace cost including employer taxes, not net or gross pay.

A person with more than one employment contract may work at most 12 hours a day. Sodra contributions have a minimum wage floor: MMA is 1,153 EUR from 1 January 2026 and 1,245 EUR from 1 January 2027 (with exceptions).
Each service or goods line should state the planned quantity, the unit rate and its basis, and a clear calculation. Example: fuel at the Ministry of Finance rate of 0.09 EUR per person per km.
Show unit cost logic, not lump totals. A 5,000 EUR training should be broken into lecturer hours, room rent, catering per participant per day, and materials per participant.

Where the call allows, an NGO budget can include administration costs, staff capacity training, cooperation and study visits, upgrades of technical equipment, and a financial audit (from direct costs if allowed, otherwise from indirect costs).
Co-financing can be cash (earned income from contracts or services, 1.2% personal income tax donations, business support, membership fees, municipal co-financing) or in-kind volunteer work.

The promoter sets the volunteer hourly rate case by case, based on usual pay for that type of work, between the minimum and average hourly wage or the pay for that position. Ministry of Finance fixed rates also exist for volunteer in-kind contributions.

Keep supporting documents for every cost: service contract and acceptance act, invoice, internal orders (for example travel allowances), payroll records (contract, job description, timesheet, payroll sheet), travel documents (tickets, invoices, car use agreement, fuel receipts with the organisation's details).

Common budget errors: unclear link between costs and activities, no basis for amounts, costs not needed by activities, 12 months budgeted instead of the project period, full-day catering for events under 4 hours, inflated rates, no reason for pricier items, fixed assets not allowed by the guidelines, services and goods mixed up, arithmetic errors, one person as both manager and performer under an individual activity certificate.

More common errors: budgeting proposal preparation, forgetting leave compensation, no rate justification, services unrelated to the project, vague bases like 'phone survey' or 'per contract' without date and number, offers not matching the budget, broken formulas, exceeding the maximum grant, wrong fixed rates, participant numbers or event length not matching the budget.

Describe and justify every budget line so evaluators have no doubts, link each cost to activities and results, follow the call rules, plan rationally at market prices, and never double-fund costs already covered by state, municipal, EU or other support.
SME status depends on staff headcount, annual turnover and annual balance sheet total. The applicant, partner enterprises and linked enterprises are all assessed.

SME thresholds: medium under 250 staff (annual work units) and turnover up to 50 million EUR or balance sheet up to 43 million EUR; small under 50 staff and up to 10 million EUR turnover or balance sheet; micro under 10 staff and up to 2 million EUR turnover or balance sheet.

SME status is judged over the reporting year and the two years before. The worked cases show that a one-year change does not alter status; it changes only after two consecutive years above or below the thresholds.
Many 2021-2027 measures have separate budgets for the Capital region (Sostinės regionas, SR) and the Central and Western Lithuania region (VVL). Check which envelope your location falls into.
Innovation Agency calls use either a competition (konkursas) or selection by planning (atranka planavimo būdu).

Young farmer loans: an individual must be 18-40 (not yet 41 on the application date), have a farm holding and farm registered in their name, be setting up as holder for the first time, and have farming competence or at least one year of practical experience.

Young farmer loans for legal persons: the holding is registered in the company's name, participants and the management body are no older than 40, the sole manager and at least 50% of board members and of participants have farming competence, and the company is setting up a holding for the first time.
Small and medium farm development: at least 1 year of activity, at least 50% of income from agriculture, and economic size (VED) of 16,001-30,000 EUR.

Agricultural investment measures pay a share of eligible costs (40%, 50% or 65% depending on the measure). Young farmers get 15 or 20 percentage points more, capped at 80% in the sustainable investments measure.

Before applying, check your data in public registers: agricultural holding, farm, animal and machinery data; legal right to the real estate registered at Registrų centras; company data (financial statements, shareholders, capital increases) at Registrų centras and in the legal entity participants system (JADIS).
The applicant must have no debts to the state budget or the State Social Insurance Fund (Sodra).

Fill every relevant field in the applicant section. In the project section give the location, stages, need, chosen solution and expected result, keep the duration within the measure's maximum, and show fit with priorities and objectives.

List only costs eligible under the measure rules. Include VAT in the total project value, stay within set rates, choose the lowest price in the supplier offer, and attach 3 comparable commercial offers for each cost.
The total project value must include VAT, and the financing sources must add up to the value with VAT.
Detail own, public and private financing sources. The source 'support funds' (paramos lėšos) can be used only if the project runs in more than one stage.

Land areas stated in the application must match declared areas. Justify innovativeness with productivity or quality gains, before and after comparison, and a described analogue or substitute with sources.
Set monitoring indicators you can reach. Sanctions can apply if committed indicators are not met.
Applicants commit to insure assets, publicise investments made with support, give auditors and controllers access during and after the project, and provide information.
All persons must sign data processing consents, including every shareholder of the applicant and linked companies.

Some measures require a business plan justifying the investment technically, financially, economically, socially and environmentally. Back financial forecasts with competitor price analysis, pricing assumptions and the market situation.
